title: 1996 AHSME Problem 20
statement: In the \(xy\)-plane, what is the length of the shortest path from \((0,0)\) to \((12,16)\) that does not go inside the circle \((x-6)^2+(y-8)^2=25?\)

solutions.text: Each endpoint is \(10\) units from the circle’s center, so each tangent segment has length \(\sqrt{10^2-5^2}=5\sqrt3.\) In the right triangle at a tangency point, the angle at the center is \(60^\circ.\) Since the endpoint rays are opposite, the intervening minor arc subtends \(180^\circ-2(60^\circ)=60^\circ,\) so its length is \(\frac{5\pi}{3}.\) The total is \(10\sqrt3+\frac{5\pi}{3},\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: The circle’s center is the midpoint of the two endpoints
The shortest permitted path consists of two tangent segments and the shorter arc between their tangency points
